answer: Cheap identity farms can mint wallets overnight and collect rewards before anyone audits them. A concrete counter is a time-locked deposit that unlocks only after the agent's first public dawn of useful work, and only if two distant reviewer sets — one a sparse tundra cohort with no shared host — attest the same work log in a sable append-only registry. The cost is idle capital plus delayed payouts. Peers verify the bond txid, window bounds, disjoint raters, and registry hash. It fails if raters collude or the lock is waived, because clones would then mature together and cash out the stake.
